s: The twelve apostles, gathered in Jerusalem, send their teaching to the Church. Christians are to keep God's law, love their neighbour and avoid every evil.
The rich should not sit idle but read the Scriptures, which teach how to live.
A wife should obey her husband and adorn herself with good works rather than finery. Husbands should love their wives.
The qualities of a good bishop, presbyter and deacon, and how a bishop should care for his people and correct sinners.
The bishop should not listen to false accusations. Each should keep his place, and the sinner who repents should be received.
The bishop should receive repentant sinners with mercy, as Christ does, and restore them to the Church.
No one should be condemned without proof. To cast out an innocent person is worse than murder.
The people should honour their bishops and bring offerings to the Church, which the deacons distribute.
The deacon serves the bishop and does nothing without him. The clergy deserve support and honour.
The bishop should judge every matter justly and patiently, hearing both sides before he decides.
Christians should forgive their neighbours seventy times seven, and the deacon should ask before the Eucharist if anyone holds anger.
Bishops should be peacemakers. How the faithful are to be seated in church and how the bishop blesses the people.
Christians should keep away from pagan gatherings, the theatre and pagan songs, and should work hard like the ant.
A widow should be at least sixty, of good works, and devoted to prayer. Widows should not gossip or wander from house to house.
Women should not baptize, as Christ did not give this to his mother or the women disciples.
Lay people should not take on the work of the priesthood, such as baptizing or offering.
On true widows and those who only bear the name. The work of deaconesses, and how the bishop anoints the newly baptized.
Childless Christians should adopt orphans, and fathers should let their sons marry orphan girls.
Bishops should provide for widows, orphans and the poor, and those who receive should pray for their givers.
Widows and the poor should receive gifts with thanksgiving and trust God for their food.
The bishop should refuse offerings from those who live by sin, such as unjust traders and oppressors.
Fathers should teach their children the Lord's commands and a trade, and correct them firmly in their youth.
Christian servants should obey their masters, whether believers or not. Masters should love believing servants as brothers.
Virgins should not make a vow until they have proven themselves.
Christians brought to trial for Christ should be supported by the faithful. Martyrdom is to be endured with courage, as Christ endured.
The martyrs are to be honoured, like James and Stephen.
Christians should not go to feasts with dancing and worldly songs, but sing psalms in the church.
Christians should not swear by false gods or even speak their names, for idols are the work of men's hands.
The feasts of the Church: Christmas, Epiphany, Holy Week and the story of the Passion.
How to fix the date of Easter, and the fast and vigil of Holy Week.
Bishops should keep away from heretics and unbelievers, who will face God's judgment.
How Satan stirred up divisions in the Church, beginning with Simon Magus, whom Peter opposed.
The true faith in the Holy Trinity as the apostles preached it, and warnings against the heresies of their time.
Gather in church to read the Scriptures for those who have died, celebrate the Eucharist, and give alms for them.
Choose the way of life. Work with your hands and give thanks to God. Do not practise magic.
The prayers of thanksgiving over the chrism and the oil.
The angels praise God without ceasing, and the Church joins in their song.
Rest on the Sabbath and Lord's Day to hear the Scriptures and remember the sufferings of Christ.
Those who wish to be baptized must first be taught the faith, renounce Satan and confess Christ.
The prayer of the priest over the baptismal water.
The prayer over the chrism, and the newly baptized pray the Our Father.
The prayer of the newly baptized, asking for the Holy Spirit to dwell in them.
The names of the first bishops ordained by the apostles in each city, beginning with James the brother of the Lord in Jerusalem.

i: The Ethiopic Didascalia (“teaching”) is a church order in 43 chapters that presents itself as the instruction of the twelve apostles gathered in Jerusalem, sent out by the hand of Clement. The Ethiopian Church counts it in its broader New Testament. It is a version of the first books of the Apostolic Constitutions, a Greek collection made in Syria around AD 380, which itself reworked the older Didascalia of the Apostles from the third century.

It speaks to every member of the Church in turn: how bishops should judge fairly, receive sinners who repent and care for widows and orphans; how deacons serve; how husbands, wives, children and servants should live; how to keep Sunday, the feasts and the fast of Holy Week; how to honour the martyrs and pray for the dead; and how to avoid heresies, with stories of Simon Magus. It ends with prayers for baptism and a list of the first bishops ordained by the apostles.
What to expect: long chapters of practical, often stern advice, full of quotations from the Old and New Testaments. The Catholic Church does not count it among the books of the Bible.
